nate-herk.name: Nate Herk
nate-herk.expect_per_week: 4-7 uploads, nearly all substantive standalone videos
nate-herk.note: Descriptions are heavy with affiliate/funnel links; real substance is usually 2-3 paragraphs below the promo block.

matt-wolfe.name: Matt Wolfe
matt-wolfe.expect_per_week: 5-7 uploads; the 'AI News:' roundup is the flagship
matt-wolfe.note: Titles starting '#ad' are sponsored. Weight comparative tests over single-tool praise.

nate-b-jones.name: Nate B Jones
nate-b-jones.expect_per_week: ~14 uploads, but roughly half are shorts
nate-b-jones.note: Shorts are hashtag-stuffed in the title. The long videos are where the actual argument lives.

all-in.name: All-In Podcast
all-in.expect_per_week: 1 flagship episode + 6-10 clips cut from that same episode
all-in.note: CLIPS ARE REDUNDANT with the flagship - they are excerpts of it, not new content. Take the flagship (the long multi-topic title) and drop the clips. If clips are useful at all, it is only as a signal of which segments the editors thought mattered most.

tom-bilyeu.name: Tom Bilyeu
tom-bilyeu.note: Titles are engineered for alarm; the reasoning inside is more measured. Most days are reaction content with low durable value - be selective.
